title: Operator ChefKit: lightweight admin primitives & flow templates
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Goal: Ship a small, composable library of admin primitives (start/stop/scale/check) and opinionated flow templates that let support engineers turn runbooks into idempotent, auditable tasks. The ChefKit is intended to reduce cognitive load for on-call and support by providing: compact step libraries, CLI helpers that wrap permissions and audit events, a lightweight JSON/YAML task manifest format, and easy mapping to existing runbook steps. Scope: core primitives for compute (deployer hooks), routing (smart fallbacks), cache and KV maintenance, and incident-safe rollbacks. Out of scope: full UI console integration (follow-up), broad RBAC design for tenants (separate project). Success metric: reduce mean time to resolution for common maintenance tasks by 30% in Q2 trials and cut ad-hoc support playbook authoring time in half.
acceptance_criteria: ChefKit library published to internal PyPI and NPM registries with versioned artifact
Three canonical flow templates implemented: cache-eviction, model-variant-rollback, and worker-pool-resize
CLI glue exposes `chef run` and emits structured audit events to the ops-audit sink (schema v1)
Runbook-to-task conversion guide (Confluence) and a sample converted runbook used in a dry-run with on-call team
End-to-end smoke test: execute template in staging, verify idempotency, verify cleanup hooks
implementation_steps: Design JSON task manifest schema (fields: steps[], idempotency_key, safe_mode, rollback_steps)
Implement core primitives in Python: check_node_health, drain_pool, clear_prefix_cache, promote_model_variant
Implement CLI: chef init, chef run --manifest <file>, chef dry-run, chef audit --tail
Hook audit emission to ops-audit (Kafka topic) and add minimal schema validation
Create three template manifests and unit/integration tests; add CI job to run staging smoke tests
Coordinate with on-call rotation (rotate coverage for dry-run) and collect feedback
decisions: Language: Python chosen for primitives (batteries for internal infra) and a thin JS shim will be provided for front-end teams—trade-off: single-language simplicity vs cross-team preference
Manifest format: JSON first, YAML wrappers supported via CLI. Decision driven by easier schema validation and machine-editing in pipelines.

Audit design: emit structured events to existing ops-audit Kafka topic (keep schema stable v1). Trade-off: quicker integration vs longer-term event evolution; we'll version events and include schema_url in payload.
Idempotency: mandate an idempotency_key at manifest top-level; primitives must be safe to re-run. Cost: extra implementation overhead but critical for reliability.
blockers: Ops-audit schema finalization required (security needs to sign off) - contact: security@redwood.ai
Staging infra quota: dedicated test GPU pool availability for model-variant-rollback testing (request submitted to infra team)
